business_model.answer: A donor-supported 501(c)(3) nonprofit; the service is free. It asks users for donations, tribute gifts and planned gifts, and links out to partners (GoFundMe, Meal Train, Instacart, gift cards) for families' own needs. Its privacy policy also lists advertising and marketing as a use of data. Annual revenue was about $10.6 million (FY2025), 97% contributions.

unique_value_proposition.answer: Update everyone at once about a loved one's health and gather support, so no one goes through a health journey alone.

evidence.quote: Communicate to everyone all at once in a safe and private space, relieving the burden of individually updating people.

retain_customers.answer: No subscription or contract. People keep coming back for the community: comments and messages of support, notifications when a page updates, help requests that get matched, and journaling; they report people feel less alone after six months of use.

privacy_data_consent.answer: The page creator picks Public, Semi-Private (the default: any signed-in user can see) or Private. Health details are collected only if users post them; CaringBridge says it does not sell health data but shares some data for targeted advertising, which state laws may count as a sale. Pages are deleted by emailing them and full deletion can take up to 90 days.
